Before you add anything

An add-on is a text file your agent reads. A Skill is written instructions plus settings. It cannot run code or a command on your computer, because Archie has nowhere to run one.

An add-on cannot give your agent a new service or ability. Those come from us in an app update, or from a service you connect yourself on the Connections tab, under Something else.

Friendly

Says it like a friend would, with the time still on the first line.

just give me the time2:15. Same room as last week.

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Friendly

Friendly is the peer voice. Where Warm Companion is the steady one that takes weight off you, Friendly stands level with you: the organized friend who says the thing and does not make a production of it. It writes in contractions and ordinary words, skips the corporate opener entirely, and keeps the warmth in the wording rather than in extra length, so the time of your meeting is still on the first line. Praise is specific or it does not happen. It is honest rather than agreeable: if a plan is thin it says so and offers the fix in the same message, and when it gets something wrong it says so in three words instead of a paragraph of apology. It reads your mood and follows it, so clipped messages get short answers and bad news arrives first with what to do about it right behind.

Calendar Manager

Your calendar, without opening your calendar.

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Calendar Manager

Your agent reads your calendar, on Google or Outlook, and drafts changes to it in chat. It can tell you what's coming up, find open time in your own week, and write up a new event, a reschedule, or a cancellation. Every create, update, and delete is a proposal you approve in chat first; nothing lands on your calendar until you say yes. Two limits worth knowing before you install. A new or changed event carries a title, a description, a start, and an end, and nothing else, so guests, a location, a video link, all-day and repeating events are still something you add in the calendar itself; your agent will say so and tell you the one step that finishes the job. And it sees only your own calendar, so it can find your free time but cannot tell you whether anyone else is free. Reading needs no approval, though a very full stretch comes back in pieces, and your agent will say a range is fuller than it could see rather than call the rest of it clear.

Email Manager

Your inbox, answered from the chat you’re already in.

Try saying

Reply to Dana and say I’ll have it over by FridayAnything from Jack this week?

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Email Manager

Ask and it looks. "What's my latest email?", "anything from Jack this week?", "what did I send Todd about the invoice?" It searches every connected account by sender, subject, words, or date, across your inbox, your archive, and your sent mail.

Ask it to reply and it drafts. "Reply to Dana and say I'll have it over by Friday" writes it in your voice and puts it in the chat as a card: send as-is, edit it, see other versions, or send later at a time you pick. One set to go later calls itself off if they write back first, and comes back to you instead. It works on any message in the mailbox, even ones from before you installed it.

Or start one from nothing. "Email Keller and say let's get lunch soon" writes it and hands you the same card, with the address and the subject on it to check first. Give it an address and it uses that one. Give it a name and it looks that person up in your own mailbox, so the only address it can offer is one you have already written to or heard from. Finding nobody, it asks you for the address rather than guessing.

Meanwhile it watches. New mail is read as it arrives, and you decide how much of it is worth a message: only what needs an answer from you, anything a real person wrote, or everything that got past your ignore list. What needs answering comes with a draft; the rest is one line saying what it is, with a button in case you want to reply anyway. You choose which inboxes it watches, what to never hear about, and how often it checks.

If you checked Let it tidy up, it can move mail out of your inbox, which is your mail app's archive and puts back in one word. It can never delete anything.

Works with any email account connected on the agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files.

More about Concise

Concise is one rule enforced hard: say it in the fewest words that are still complete. No preamble, no restating the question, no closing pleasantry unless you open with one. Answers come back as short lines and bullets rather than paragraphs, so a day reads like a schedule and a total reads like a number. It is the voice for someone who already knows what they want and is reading on a phone between two other things. Brevity stops where meaning starts: it will not drop a deadline, a cost, or a warning to save a line, and anything that cannot be undone still gets one short sentence and a wait for your yes.

More about Bills & Subscriptions

The job nobody wants: knowing what is about to charge you, and what is still charging you for something you stopped using. Tell your agent “the design seat is $59.99 monthly on the 3rd”, or “Netflix is $15.49 monthly on the 3rd”, and it keeps the date, rolls it forward as each one is paid, and warns you before the next. Autopay bills roll themselves, because nobody thinks to mention a charge that happened on its own. Ask what a month costs and get the arithmetic across weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly, done properly. With Email Manager (or another skill that reads your mail) installed, it will go and find the subscriptions you forgot to mention. It never pays anything and never cancels anything; it remembers the date and tells you in time.

Calm Anchor

Low pressure. One thing at a time.

I didn't do any of the things I said I would.That's alright. Nothing on that list broke. Two of them weren't really necessary anyway. Want me to just delete those? Then it's one thing, not six.

Every add-on is included with Archie.

Download Archie
More about Calm Anchor

Calm Anchor is for overloaded days and overloaded brains. It shows you the single next thing instead of the whole list, and it makes that thing small enough that starting is easy. A missed task is information, not a failure, so "you were supposed to" appears nowhere in it. It offers to cut before it offers to reschedule, because most overwhelmed lists are full of items that were never actually important and someone has to say that out loud. The pace stays low: short replies, no stacked exclamation points, no urgency you did not bring with you. When a day genuinely is a lot it says so, because being told "yeah, that's a lot" is more grounding than being told it is manageable. And if something sounds like real distress it stops organizing entirely and points you to a crisis line, your doctor, or emergency services.

More about Hype Coach

Hype Coach is for anyone chasing something with a date on it: a lift, a launch, a deadline, a habit that keeps quietly dying in a notes app. It reacts to what you did before it gets to what is next, and its praise is specific or it does not happen, because "third session this week" lands and "great job" is noise by the second time you read it. Its real work is the drift. Push the same task three times and it says so, once, kindly, and then asks what is actually in the way instead of rescheduling around it a fourth time. Then it shrinks the next step until starting is almost automatic: not "work on the deck" but "open the deck and write the title slide." It challenges and it does not shame, because you are not lazy, something is in the way, and finding it is the job.

Setting up Revenue Watch

  1. Make the key at Stripe, under Developers, API keys, and press Create restricted key. Set Read on Charges, PaymentIntents, Invoices, Subscriptions, Customers, Disputes, and Balance transactions, and leave the rest on None.
